title.en: Seidr: The Practice, Its Practitioners and Its Taboo
title.zh: 賽德巫術：其儀式、施行者與禁忌

region.en: The seiðr-platform across the Norse world (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 北歐各地的賽德法臺（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: Evidence c. 900-1200 CE (eddic, sagas, law-codes); the law-codes' seiðr-clauses (Gragas, the Gulathing-law)

source.work: Eiriks saga rauda (the Thorbjorg seance); Ynglinga saga (Odin's seiðr); Gragas and the Gulathing-law (the seiðr-clauses); Erik Segersäll's seiðr at Lejre (Thietmar of Merseburg)

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The corpus's magic-system in full practice-documentation: seiðr is the spellcraft of sitting (the high-seat ritual, the staff, the varðlokur song, the trance-vision); its practitioners are overwhelmingly female (the völva, the traveling seeress) with Odin as the male exception - and its social taboo is sexual: the ergi-clause, the accusation that seiðr unmanns its male performer (Loki's charge against Odin at the flyting; the law-codes' clauses). The record is the myth-system's practice-file: method, performers, fee, taboo, and the Christianity that ended it.
summary.zh: 語料中魔法體系的完整實踐記錄：賽德是一種「坐著」施行的咒術（高座儀式、法杖、瓦爾德魯庫咒歌、出神異象）；施行者以女性為主（女先知、雲遊占卜者），男性僅奧丁為例外——而其社會禁忌涉及性別：ergi（性變態）條款指控賽德會使男性施行者「失去男子氣概」（洛基在吵罵中以此攻擊奧丁；法典中亦有相關條款）。此記錄是神話體系的實踐檔案：方法、施行者、酬勞、禁忌，以及終結它的基督教。

texts.canonical_translation: Islenzk Fornrit editions; Thietmar per paraphrase; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The seiðr-record is the myth corpus's practice-file, and this expanded node documents the system's full anatomy. The method: seiðr is performed sitting ('the? - 'high-seat? - 'of? - 'the? - 'ritual? - the seid-hjallr of Eirik's saga), with the staff (the völva's gandur), the feast (the seid-meal of animal hearts), the costume (the blue-black cloak, the beaded headband, the brass-knobbed staff), and the song: the varðlokur - 'the? - 'songs? - 'required? - 'for? - the? - spellwork? - the trance summoned and completed by chanted formula, the spirits arriving to answer questions ('many? - 'spirits? - 'had? - 'come? - 'and? - 'found? - the? - song? - fair).

The practitioners: overwhelmingly women - the völva (the staff-bearer) traveling farm to farm in the famine-winter, the fee and the feast her wage; and the male exception, Odin himself: Ynglinga saga's clause ('Odin? - 'knew? - 'the? - 'art? - 'of? - seiðr? - 'and? - 'with? - 'it? - 'he? - 'could? - 'know? - men's? - fates? - and? - bring? - them? - the? - deaths? - he? - chose? - 'the? - god as the practice's first male performer, with the ergi-taboo attached: 'at? - 'this? - 'art? - 'there? - was? - 'such? - shame? - 'that? - 'men? - 'thought? - it? - 'unmanly? - to? - learn? - it? - 'and? - it? - 'was? - 'taught? - to? - the? - priestesses? - the taboo's doctrine: the ergi-clause (the flyting's charge: 'thou? - 'didst? - 'work? - 'witchcraft? - 'in? - woman's? - shape? - 'on? - Samsey? - the accusation that seiðr unmans its male performer), documented also in the law-codes (the Gragas and Gulathing clauses on seiðr and ergi as outlawry-offences).

The record's cultural functions are the practice-documentation doctrine (the corpus's magic-system documented with its method, costume, song, fee and stage - the fullest practice-record in the north's sources) and the gender-taboo doctrine: seiðr's power is women's power, and its male adoption is legally obscene - the myth-system's gender-structure stated in law as well as story. And the Christianity-clause: the law-codes' Christian-era amendments outlawed seiðr outright ('the? - 'Christian? - law? - 'made? - the? - seiðr-worker? - an? - outlaw? - the practice ended by statute. In the atlas, the record anchors the magic-system-practice family: each a tradition's spellcraft documented method-side; the Norse one is distinctive in the ergi-clause.

For the database, this expanded node documents the practice behind three records: Gullveig-Heid (the mythic charter), the völva-seance (the Greenland performance) and Baldr's dreams (the god's own consultation).

title.en: Heimskringla: The Kings' Sagas from Myth to History
title.zh: 《王環》：從神話到歷史的王者薩迦

region.en: Norway and the Norse realms (symbolic pin at Trondheim)
region.zh: 挪威與北歐諸邦（象徵性定位於特隆赫姆）

texts.period: Heimskringla c. 1225-1235; principal MS AM 41 4to (Kringla leaf); English: Laing 1844

source.work: Snorri Sturluson, Heimskringla (complete: Ynglinga saga through Magnus Erlingsson's saga); English: Laing 1844

texts.license: Public domain (Laing 1844); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Snorri's kings' history as a single document: sixteen sagas running from the mythic opening (Ynglinga saga: Odin's migration, the euhemerist charter, the Yngling death-catalog) through the viking kings (Harald Fairhair's unification, the conversion-kings Olaf Tryggvason and Olaf Haraldsson) to the medieval dynasties - the myth-to-history arc of a whole kingdom, in which the gods are the kings' ancestors and the myths are the dynasty's charter. The record is the corpus's great reception-document: mythology as royal history.
summary.zh: 斯諾里的王者史作為單一文獻：十六部薩迦自神話開篇（尤恩格林加薩迦：奧丁遷徙、猶赫麥爾主義憲章、英格林死亡清單），經維京諸王（統一挪威的金髮哈拉爾、皈依之王奧拉夫·特里格瓦松與奧拉夫·哈拉爾松），直至中世紀王朝——一個王國自神話到歷史的完整弧線，其中諸神即國王的祖先，神話即王朝的憲章。此記錄是語料最宏大的接受史文獻：神話作為王家歷史。

narrative.en:
Heimskringla - 'the circle of the world' (its opening words) - is the myth corpus's great reception-document, and this record holds the arc whole. The mythic opening: Ynglinga saga's euhemerist charter (the Aesir from Asia, Odin's migration, the temple-endowments, the death-laws, the Yngling death-catalog quoted from Thjodolfr's Ynglingatal) - the gods historicized as migrating chiefs, the dynasty's ancestors documented from the god-house of Uppsala. The viking middle: Halfdan the Black's dreams (the prose-history's own prophecy-motifs), Harald Fairhair's unification and his hair-vow, the conversion-kings (Olaf Tryggvason's fall at Svolder in the year of Iceland's conversion; Olaf Haraldsson's martyrdom at Stiklestad and the incorruption at Nidaros) - the mythic motifs (dreams, omens, the martyr-cult) running inside the political history.

The medieval close: Magnus the Good and Harald Hardrada (the varangian king, dying at Stamford Bridge in 1066 - the saga's last great battle-date), down to Magnus Erlingsson - the dynasty's history continuous from Odin to the 12th century. The record's cultural functions are the reception-doctrine (myth converted into royal history - the euhemerist method deployed for legitimacy: the kings descend from gods whose divinity was a mistake) and the charter-doctrine: Heimskringla is the Norwegian monarchy's founding-book, its mythology the dynasty's title-deeds. And the source-method is the record's critical datum: Snorri quotes the skaldic poems as his evidence (Ynglingatal, the lays of the battle-poets) - the historian citing verse as documents, the myth-corpus's own evidentiary practice.

In the atlas, the record anchors the myth-to-history family: each a tradition's charter-document converting the gods into ancestors; Snorri's is distinctive in quoting its own verse-sources. For the database, this whole-text node complements the Ynglinga-record and the king-records it feeds: here the kingdom's arc runs whole, god to king.

The compilation's architecture completes the record: sixteen sagas in one frame (the opening words 'Heimskringla' - the circle of the world - naming the whole as a ring), with the mythic opening and the Christian close bracketing the viking middle - the kingdom's arc designed as a document, not a chronicle. And the conversion-clause completes the myth-history junction: the two Olafs' martyrdoms and miracles are told in the same evidentiary style as Odin's migration, so the myth-register and the hagiographic register are one continuous method - the king's body as the realm's collateral from heathen sacrifice to Christian shrine.

 The compilation's evidentiary method completes the record: Snorri names and quotes his skaldic sources in the text (Ynglingatal for the Ynglings, the battle-lays for the viking kings), so the myth-to-history arc is documented with its own apparatus - the historian citing verse as documents, which is the myth corpus's own evidentiary practice institutionalized. And the compilation's afterlife completes the corpus: Heimskringla became the Norwegian kingdom's founding-book (its copy-history running through the medieval state)s hands), the mythology as the dynasty)s title-deeds - the reception-document that made the gods the kings) ancestors in law as well as in story.

title.en: Christianization and Mythic Reinterpretation: How the North Re-Read Its Gods
title.zh: 基督教化與神話再詮釋：北方如何重讀自己的神明

region.en: The converted north (symbolic pin at Jelling, Denmark)
region.zh: 皈依後的北方（象徵性定位於丹麥耶林）

source.work: Jelling stones; Gosforth cross; Islendingabok; Snorri's Prose Edda prologue and Gylfaginning frame; Adam of Bremen

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The north's conversion did not delete its mythology - it re-read it. The record documents the reinterpretation-strategies in sequence: conversion-monuments that keep the old dead alongside the new faith (Jelling), carved mythologies in Christian stone (Gosforth), constitutional conversions with exceptions (Godafoss), the learned-Christian frame that preserved the myths as poetry (Snorri's illusion-frame and euhemerism), and the moralization of the old cult in the converted sagas (Sorla thattr's necklace; Hrafnkels saga's silent Freyr). The record is the corpus's reception-history in one document: myth surviving by reinterpretation.
summary.zh: 北方的皈依並未刪除其神話，而是對其重新詮釋。此記錄依序記錄了各種再詮釋策略：讓舊日亡者與新信仰並存的皈依紀念碑（耶林）、雕入基督教石材的神話（戈斯福斯）、附有例外條款的憲政皈依（眾神瀑布）、以「詩藝」之名保存神話的基督教學術框架（斯諾里的幻象框架與猶赫麥爾主義），以及皈依後薩迦對舊崇拜的道德化改寫（《索爾拉短篇》的項鏈；《赫拉芬克爾薩迦》中沉默的弗雷）。此記錄是語料接受史的單一文獻：神話因再詮釋而存續。

texts.language: Old Norse / Old Icelandic; Latin; Old Danish (runic)

narrative.en:
The Christianization-record is the myth corpus's reception-history, and its doctrine is survival-by-reinterpretation. The monuments: Jelling's two stones (father's heathen memorial, son's conversion-charter with the carved Christ - one generation apart, the transition's speed documented in granite) and Gosforth's cross (Ragnarok-panels beside the crucifixion, the two end-times read together on one stone) - the conversion's visual theology, carved for mixed congregations.

The constitutions: the Althing's arbitration of 1000 (one law and one faith, with three exceptions: infant exposure, horse-flesh, private sacrifice if secret - the old cult licensed into privacy) and Thorgeirr's own temple-cleansing (the idols into Godafoss) - conversion as statute, with the exceptions later annulled. The learned frame: Snorri's two-part strategy - the euhemerist prologue (the Aesir as migrating chiefs whose divinity was a mistake) and the Gylfaginning illusion-frame (the catechism taught in a hall that vanishes) - the myths preserved as poetry ('for? - 'the? - 'needs? - 'of? - poetry) in a Christendom that burned heretics elsewhere.

The moralizations: the converted sagas re-reading the old cult - Sorla thattr's necklace (Freyja's jewel re-narrated as the engine of human war, ended by the new king's faith), Hrafnkels saga's Freyfaxi (the cult's terror-claims tested empirically and found political - the god's silence as the thesis), and the conversion-sagas' mission-kings (Olaf Tryggvason's fire-and-baptism; the poets' conversion-contracts). The record's cultural functions are the reinterpretation-strategy doctrine (each layer a different survival-strategy: monument, carve, statute, frame, moralize) and the survival-doctrine: the myth corpus exists at all because the converted north kept re-reading it. In the atlas, the record anchors the conversion-reception family: each a tradition's faith-change and its mythic residue; the Norse one is distinctive in the learned frame's honesty.

For the database, this node documents the corpus's own history: why the myths survive, and in whose service.

The record's method completes the reception-doctrine: each layer is documented from its own evidence (runes for Jelling, sculpture for Gosforth, law-texts for the Althing, prose for Snorri's frame and the converted sagas), so the reception-history is built multi-media - the myth tradition's survival documented in stone, statute and story together. And the survival-thesis completes the corpus: the myth database exists because the converted north chose re-reading over deletion - the critical-digital-history lesson written in the corpus's own history.

 The record's lesson for the database is its own thesis: the myth corpus survives in this database because the converted north chose re-reading over deletion - the five strategies (monument, carve, statute, frame, moralize) are the corpus)s own survival-machinery, each documented from its own medium (runes, sculpture, law-text, prose frame, converted saga). And the digital-history lesson completes it: the reception-layers are searchable as a stratum of their own - the myths) truth-conditions change by layer, and the database)s provenance-fields (manuscript, reading, sensitivity) document exactly those conditions, layer by layer.

title.en: Laxdaela saga: The Family Saga of Guðrún's Four Dreams
title.zh: 《拉克斯峽谷薩迦》：古德倫四夢的家族薩迦

region.zh: 冰島拉克斯峽谷與達利爾

texts.period: Laxdaela saga 13th century (events set c. 890-1030); principal MSS 14th c. and vellum fragments; English: Muriel Press, The Laxdale Saga, 1899

source.work: Laxdaela saga (complete); ed. Islenzk Fornrit V (1935); English: Muriel Press, The Laxdale Saga, London 1899

texts.license: Public domain (Press 1899); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The great family saga of the Laxardal: the settlement-generation's gold (Melkorka the Irish princess, sold as a thrall and ransomed), the rise of the Össur-line, and the saga's famous core - Guðrún Ósvífsdóttir's four dreams (the water-laden hat, the silver ring from the lake, the gold ring, and the battle-woman's helm) interpreted as her four marriages, and her marriages' tragedies: Kjartan and Bolli's friendship broken, the killing, Bolli's slaying of Kjartan, the vengeance, and the saga's last word - Guðrún's answer to the question 'whom do you love most?' ('I? - 'was? - 'worst? - 'to? - him? - whom? - 'I? - loved? - most). The record is the mythic motifs' social register: dreams as prophecy, omen-reading as daily practice, and fate as marriage.
summary.zh: 拉克斯峽谷的偉大家族薩迦：拓殖世代之黃金（愛爾蘭公主梅爾科爾卡淪為奴隸後被贖回）、奧蘇爾一族的興起，以及薩迦著名的核心——古德倫·奧斯維夫斯多蒂爾的四個夢（盛水之帽、湖中銀環、金環、持械女武者之盔），被解為她的四段婚姻；而婚姻的悲劇隨之而來：基亞爾坦與博利的友誼破裂、殺戮、博利弒基亞爾坦、復仇，以及薩迦的結語——當被問「你最愛誰」時，古德倫答道：「我最愛的人，待他最壞。」此記錄是神話母題的社會層面：夢即預言、解兆為日常實踐、命運即婚姻。

texts.canonical_translation: Muriel Press, The Laxdale Saga, London 1899 (public domain); Islenzk Fornrit V

narrative.en:
Laxdaela saga is the family-sagas' masterpiece of fate-as-marriage, and its mythic register is the dreams. The dream-interpretation: Guðrún's four dreams told to Gestr the wise ('the? - 'dream-interpreter? - 'of? - the? - saga) and read as her four marriages - the hat heavy with water (the first marriage, weeping), the silver ring from the lake (the second, lost), the gold ring (the third, the king's? - 'the? - 'gold? - 'ring? - 'a? - king's? - son), and the helm of the battle-woman ('the? - 'fourth? - 'dream: 'I? - 'fancied? - I? - wore? - a? - helm? - 'of? - 'the? - 'wolf? - - the valkyrie-helm dream read as Kjartan: 'a? - 'warrior? - 'woman? - 'shall? - be? - 'thy? - fate? - - the four dreams as the four fates, prophecy domesticated into marriage-counsel.

The marriages' tragedies: Guðrún wed to Thorvald (divorced by her own wit - the trouser-legs clause), then to Thord, then to Kjartan's rival Bolli (the love-triangle's politics: Kjartan abroad in Norway, engaged to the king's sister Hildigunnr, returning to find Guðrún married), the feud's escalation (Kjartan's cattle-raids on Bolli's farm, the ambush at Svinadale? - Kjartan killed by Bolli 'of? - all? - men? - 'the? - dearest? - to? - him), and the vengeance (Guðrún's sons killing Bolli - the family consuming itself).

The saga's last scene is the corpus's most quoted marriage-fate: the old Guðrún answering her son's question ('whom? - 'didst? - thou? - love? - best): 'I? - 'was? - 'worst? - 'to? - 'him? - 'whom? - 'I? - loved? - most? - - the fate-doctrine's social form: love as the engine of ruin. The record's cultural functions are the dream-prophecy doctrine (the dreams read as marriages - prophecy as household counseling, the interpreter as a professional) and the myth-in-the-social doctrine: the saga's thrall-princess (Melkorka, the Irish king's daughter sold into slavery, her identity proven by the Irish speech), the valkyrie-helm imagery and the fate-formula show the mythic motifs functioning inside ordinary family law - the myth corpus's social register. In the atlas, the record anchors the dream-fate family: each a saga reading dreams as biography; the Laxdaela one is distinctive in the four-dream sequence.

For the database, this record documents how the mythic motifs (prophecy, fate, valkyrie-imagery, gold) run in the family-sagas - the myth-tradition's everyday operation.

The saga's gold-register completes the myth-in-the-social doctrine: Melkorka's ransoming (the Irish speech proving the princess-thrall's identity) and Hrosteolf's? - Hroskarr's? - the gold-hoarding episodes document wealth as the family's fate-engine, the same gold-economy the heroic corpus theorizes operating in household law. And the women's register completes the record: Guðrún, Melkorka, Hildigunnr and thethers? - the saga's women as its plot-engines - the family saga as the myth-motifs' social laboratory, where prophecy, fate and gold run through marriage-law.

passages.text: Guðrún's four dreams were read as her four marriages: the water-laden hat (weeping), the silver ring from the lake (lost), the gold ring (a king's son), and the helm of the battle-woman - a warrior woman shall be thy fate. Asked in old age whom she loved best, Guðrún answered: 'I was worst to him whom I loved most' - love as the engine of the family's ruin.

summary.en: The saga corpus's epic of law and fate: Gunnar of Hlíðarendi, the champion who never wished to leave ('the? - 'famous? - 'slope-clause: 'how? - 'fair? - the? - slope? - 'is? - 'so? - fair? - 'to? - behold? - 'the? - 'bright? - 'wheat-field? - 'than? - 'to? - 'go? - 'under? - the? - woe - refusing exile for the land's beauty), his death at home by the law's doom (he would not bow his head), the lawyer Njál's fate-foreknowledge ('the? - 'seer-lawyer: 'this? - 'shall? - 'be? - 'thy? - death? - 'the? - 'christening? - 'of? - thy? - sons? - and? - the? - burning), and the burning at Bergþórshváll that ends the family - with Kári's survival and the vendetta's closing. The record is the mythic motifs' legal register: oath, curse, fate and prophecy running inside the courts.
summary.zh: 薩迦語料中法律與命運的史詩：赫利達倫迪的槍尼雅爾——那位不願離鄉的勇士（名句：「這山坡如此秀美，金色麥田如此悅目，寧願死在此地，也不願在異鄉屈膝」——他拒絕流亡，甘願就死於家門）、不肯低頭的死亡，以及律師尼雅爾的命運預知（「這將是你的死：為兒子行洗禮，然後迎來火焚」）——最終貝格索爾斯瓦爾的大火終結了整個家族，而卡里倖存並了結宿怨。此記錄是神話母題的法律層面：誓言、詛咒、命運與預言在法庭之內運行。

texts.canonical_translation: Sir George Dasent, The Story of Burnt Njal, Edinburgh 1861 (public domain); Islenzk Fornrit XII

narrative.en:
Njáls saga is the saga corpus's epic of law, and its mythic register is the fate-motifs running inside the courts. The oath-and-doom register: Gunnar's oath-broken feud (the oath to leave Iceland broken at the shore - the famous clause: 'how? - 'fair? - the? - slope? - 'is? - 'so? - fair? - 'to? - behold? - 'the? - 'wheat-field? - 'than? - 'to? - go? - under? - 'woe? - 'and? - 'death? - 'he? - turned? - back? - 'and? - 'the? - 'outlaw's? - doom? - executed at home: he died 'shooting? - with? - the? - bow? - 'till? - the? - string? - broke? - 'and? - 'he? - died? - 'where? - he? - stood - the land-beauty as the fate's own argument), and Njál's foreknowledge ('the? - 'lawyer's? - prophecy: 'the? - 'boy? - 'Höskuld's? - death? - 'foretold? - 'at? - his? - christening? - 'the? - christening-prophecy clause: 'this? - 'shall? - 'be? - 'his? - death: 'that? - 'he? - 'shall? - 'be? - 'slain? - 'in? - 'the? - Althing's? - law-court? - - fate foretold in the church-rite, prophecy as christening-gift).

The burning: the burning at Bergþórshváll (the saga's great atrocity: the family burned in its hall, Njál refusing to leave - 'he? - 'said? - 'he? - 'would? - 'die? - 'with? - his? - wife? - and? - sons? - the fate accepted as the lawyer's own counsel), the survival of Kári, and the vendetta's closing (the Althing's settlement and Kári's last rides). The record's cultural functions are the law-as-fate doctrine (the courts themselves as the fate's machinery: the legal outcomes - outlawry, compensation, settlement - execute the prophecies) and the fate-motif register: the saga's omens (the blood-rain, the dreams, the dead-speaking? - the ghost's warning at Hlidarendi) document the mythic motifs functioning inside legal procedure - the myth-tradition's law-court operation.

And the saga's Christianity-frame is the record's critical datum: the conversion-scene is in the saga (the Godafoss-chapters, Njál's own baptism discussed at the Thing), so the fate-motifs run inside the converted world - the mythic fate-doctrine persisting under Christian law. In the atlas, the record anchors the law-and-fate family: each a tradition's legal order run by fate-motifs; the Norse one is distinctive in the christening-prophecy and the land-beauty clause.

For the database, this record documents the mythic motifs' legal operation: oath, curse, prophecy and doom as the law-court's own machinery.

passages.text: Gunnar, outlawed, turned back at the shore: 'how fair the slope is, so fair to behold the bright wheat-field, than to go under woe and death' - and he died at home, shooting with the bow till the string broke. Njál foretold the fate at Höskuld's christening, and the fate ran through the courts to the burning at Bergþórshváll, where he said he would die with his wife and sons - the law-courts as the fate's own machinery.
